backbone: Fourier inversion reduces joint law to mixed decorrelation; assuming a nonzero correlation, a profinite profile limit and divisor amplifier yield a positive energy contradicting Matomaki-Radziwill short-interval cancellation.
quote: A profile of a nonzero mixed correlation

backbone: Extract a long prime prefix from Ford's structure of preimages, count values via simplex volumes, and show collisions are negligible by a layered shifted-prime sieve comparison.
quote: The comparison and the subsequent control of tuple multiplicities are the ingredients that turn a volume estimate into an asymptotic for distinct values.

backbone: Joint induction on dimension of bigness (full nef dimension) and positive-part numerical semiampleness, via MMP reductions to Calabi-Yau pairs, jet/Frobenius arguments, and descent along nef reduction.
quote: We prove the following two assertions together, by induction on $n$.

backbone: Write down an explicit degree-five polynomial, verify stabilization by an explicit coordinate change, and rule out coordinateness via an associated graded ring, locally nilpotent derivation and rigidity obstruction.
quote: We construct the counterexample through a hypersurface presentation of a four-variable polynomial ring. This presentation makes stabilization explicit and will also supply the filtration used to obstruct coordinateness.

backbone: Smooth two contact lines into very free conics, extend moving-pair tensors over stable-map compactification to get a global section, deduce contact transitivity, identify with adjoint variety, then twistor correspondence.
quote: The first-jet generation obtained below supplies such an immersion; we give the resulting contact moment-map classification directly.

backbone: Reduce a.e. convergence to a good-set integral bound for bounded-height inputs, summed over doubly exponential height layers; the bound is proved via a finite dyadic procedure with entropy-compression budgets.
quote: Our proof proceeds through the good-set integral estimate described next.

backbone: For polytopes, a conformal lens and holomorphic mass estimate give a feasible-simplex probability sum at least 1, identified with a simplex integral bounded by the volume product; approximation extends it.
quote: A holomorphic mass estimate turns that boundary law into a lower bound for an integral of feasible-simplex volumes over the primal body.

backbone: Lower bound: recursively build explicit word families with cheap steps and separated prime-order shifts, and a Fourier prime-product displacement inequality forces distortion; upper bound adapts the Ostrovsky-Rabani embedding.
quote: The construction below reaches the scale of the Ostrovsky--Rabani exponent.

backbone: Construct an explicit fixed-vector rule (max branch plus layered nested flats from sampled density expansions and guards), bound its expected min-over-orders payoff, then couple to the one-sample model.
quote: We construct the rule of Proposition~\ref{prop:hidden} for a fixed hidden weight vector. It uses geometric rounding and chooses with equal probability between a single-choice maximum branch and a main branch.

backbone: Give a dynamic program over polynomially many bounded-formula job sets, and prove every feasible schedule has a recursive bounded-description interval hierarchy so the program accepts it.
quote: The proof reorganizes feasible schedules into intervals whose job sets have descriptions of bounded size. A dynamic program searches a family containing polynomially many such descriptions.

backbone: Construct an explicit quasilinear reduction: sparse End-of-Line macrograph, locally evolving outer representation over group-indexed codes, composed with an algebraic inner gadget; robust decoding via a clipped-mean contradiction.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:outer-composition} assembles the main theorem from the outer representation, the port interface stated there, and the independent geometric interface. It proves universal decoding, the complete binary size bound, and rational-witness totality.

backbone: Upper bound by regrouping into n-block maps; lower bound by contradiction: a dimension deficit yields pair mass in scale bands, giving disjoint entropy-gain windows exceeding the entropy rate.
quote: We prove the upper bound before turning to the contradiction argument.

backbone: In a cyclic model, a random outer coloring (finite local lemma) plus a norm-indexed random perturbation of Behrend-type geometry avoids monochromatic progressions; then transfer to intervals and more colors.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:outer} uses them to construct the outer coloring. Section~\ref{sec:dichotomy} turns its local tests into the balanced-or-affine alternative. Section~\ref{perturb:section} introduces the norm-indexed perturbation and proves the cyclic two-color theorem.

backbone: Take a minimal counterexample, derive a strict subset-growth inequality, blow up into transitive tournaments, and contradict it with a pruning bound for binary relations and an extremal compatible-pair argument.
quote: We first suppose that a counterexample exists and choose one with minimum order and then minimum number of arcs.

backbone: Build a self-dual matroid via an ultrafilter ordinal rank and continuum-length recursion of bases, chain copies along a double ray; an independent covering forces an infinite descending ordinal sequence.
quote: In a putative independent covering, one starts with the large side of a central bundle and follows the path outward. Each successive copy of $Q$ strictly decreases the ordinal rank, an impossibility.

backbone: Attach cones on random labeled graphs to a rose; a parity criterion gives ab=1, ac=0, and counting plus planar separators give asphericity and protected roots with high probability.
quote: We first show that there is a constant \(\rho>0\) such that, with probability tending to one,

backbone: For an explicit ramified regular local ring, push an integral Bott-type class from a split divisor so it dies generically, and detect its mod-5 reduction by Picard specialization.
quote: We construct a two-dimensional ramified regular local ring $A$ of mixed characteristic $(0,5)$ for which $K_5(A)\to K_5(\Frac A)$ has a nonzero kernel.

backbone: Upper bound by interpolation; matching lower bound via perturbation identities on prescribed trees, inductive multioverlap concentration over delayed branching depths, and comparison of cavity insertions with independent hierarchical messages.
quote: Bounded perturbations yield identities for prescribed replica branching patterns. Delaying each branching depth by one level permits an induction that concentrates multioverlaps \emph{on average over branching depths}.

backbone: Prove joint tightness, identify the height limit as a GFF via reflection positivity, screening and Wick moments, then identify current clusters as canonical two-valued local sets, characterizing every subsequential limit.
quote: Our proof first obtains joint tightness, then identifies every subsequential limit as the canonical construction of \cref{thm:main}.

backbone: Reduce to finite specifications; build reducibility candidates on the sort-profile graph component by component, excluding the forbidden configuration by a relational Hurkens-paradox diagonal argument from weak normalization.
quote: If the interface can be implemented at every strongly connected component, then every legal expression of the PTS is strongly normalizing.

backbone: A random nested-table presentation is aspherical with linear filling with high probability; a hypothetical CAT(0) action yields, via energy minimization and tangent cones, a configuration contradicted by flat-square rigidity.
quote: The proof is an existence argument and does not give an effective size for $K$.

backbone: Prove H^2 >= gamma H by comparing the two-, three- and four-body terms of H^2 with an explicit rotation-averaged sum of squares, certified by exact rational arithmetic.
quote: Our argument uses rotations and angular-momentum decomposition to construct such a comparison. It starts from the normal-ordered expansion of \(H_Q^2\).

backbone: Take a bounded Gaussian formula nearly attaining the Parisi value, compile it into a QAOA word via a fixed-word tree calculus with temporary seed controls, then remove the controls.
quote: The quantum construction simulates a finite classical calculation, using temporary Gaussian seed controls and then removing them.

backbone: Construct a circle weight from stagewise-chosen divisible frequencies; an invariant projection gives convolution identities contradicted by an obstruction from sampled orbit-pair couplings; then smooth the weight to be continuous.
quote: We construct divisible integers $1=q_0\mid q_1\mid q_2\mid\cdots$ and positive costs $c_i$.

backbone: Construct an explicit 4-manifold with disc maps and framed algebraic duals; hypothetical disjoint discs give smooth cut data and formal flat-connection deformations, contradicted by a characteristic-l Frobenius-Koszul residue obstruction.
quote: We construct the input discs and their algebraic duals in an actual smooth four-manifold. The geometric conclusion needed later is conditional: any system of disjoint proper topological discs with the prescribed boundaries produces the smooth cut data

backbone: Build stationary cylinders and labelled pieces of pushouts, prove the nerve comparison for subdivided boundary and horn attachments by poset induction, then transfer model axioms and the Quillen equivalence.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:attachments} proves the nerve comparison for subdivided boundary and horn attachments, with explicit control of the monomorphic gluing legs. Section~\ref{sec:transfer} supplies the model axioms, properness, and the unit comparison for arbitrary simplicial sets.

backbone: Construct a convex hull of matrix columns from finite-field partitions: uniform compression bounds one covering entropy while Schwartz-Zippel separated rows force the dual entropy large; tuned parameters violate the inequality.
quote: For every proposed pair of universal constants, we construct origin-symmetric convex bodies that violate the corresponding covering-entropy inequality, already when the covering body is a cube.

backbone: Families Seiberg-Witten wall crossing and Taubes curves over the coefficient sphere give a nodal torus fibration; an auxiliary equal-square pair then deforms the triple to a hyperkahler endpoint.
quote: \Cref{sec:families,sec:lattice-chamber,sec:pencil} construct the torus fibration, and \Cref{sec:local-models,sec:regular-preparation,sec:auxiliary-volume} construct the auxiliary equal-square pair.

backbone: Rigidity reduces to uniform section balance; its failure yields affine convex limit models, and multi-direction models are excluded by a coercive integral inequality valid through dimension nine.
quote: Our argument identifies the dimension restriction in a quadratic coercivity estimate, whose strict positivity holds through dimension nine.

backbone: Recover boundary jets, get equal Green matrices on an exterior cap, define a maximal local isometry, and show a putative interior frontier point extends, contradicting maximality.
quote: They define a maximal local isometry with a unitary bundle identification; Section~\ref{sec:boundary} prepares coordinates and harmonic frames at any putative frontier point.

backbone: Failure of a uniform affine-approximation rate yields, by rescaling and compactness, an entire nonaffine limiting solution; an extremal Jensen-defect envelope contact argument forces it to be affine.
quote: First we reduce failure of a uniform power rate for affine approximation to an entire nonaffine solution of a limiting equation. Then we prove that the estimates inherited by that limit force it to be affine.
